_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: The Quran tells of brothers who owned a fine garden. Their father used to share its harvest with the poor. They planned to pick it all at dawn, quietly, so no one in need could ask for a share. Watch what they found.
intro.curious: The Quran tells of brothers who owned a fine garden. They planned to pick it all at dawn, quietly, so no one in need could ask for a share. Watch what they found.

muslim.situation: You've saved money from a part-time job for a year. A charity at your mosque is raising funds for families who can't afford food this winter.

options.label: Give nothing: you worked hard for it.
options.feedback: You did work hard. The brothers in the garden thought the same way. Next you'll see what Islam says about whose wealth it really is.

options.label: Give a little, only if people will see it.
options.feedback: Giving to be seen loses what giving is for. The teaching explains.

options.label: Work out the zakat due on your savings and give it, quietly.
options.feedback: That's exactly the pillar: a set share of savings, given to those in need, without fuss.

options.label: Give something now, and promise yourself to give properly later.
options.feedback: A good start. Zakat isn't left to mood, though: it's a fixed share, due each year.

curious.situation: You've saved money from a part-time job for a year. A local food bank is asking for help for families who can't afford food this winter.

options.label: Give nothing: you worked hard for it.
options.feedback: That's a common feeling. The brothers in the garden felt the same. Next you'll see what Islam teaches about wealth.

options.label: Give a little, mainly so people see it.
options.feedback: Islam treats giving to be seen as giving that loses its point. The teaching explains.

options.label: Give a fair share of your savings, quietly.
options.feedback: That's the idea behind zakat: a set share of savings given each year to those in need.

options.label: Give something now and promise more later.
options.feedback: A good start. In Islam this giving is a fixed duty each year, not left to mood.

quran.about: God tells how the garden's owners swore to reap it in the morning without leaving a share, and how something from their Lord passed over it while they slept.
They admitted they had done wrong, and turned to blaming one another.
Charity taken from people's wealth purifies them and helps them grow.
God names who zakat is for: the poor, the needy, those in debt, the traveller in need, and others.
Spending in God's way is like a seed that grows seven ears, with a hundred grains in each.

hadith.about: Charity does not make wealth less.
Zakat is one of the five pillars Islam is built on.

insights.text: Zakat is not the same as general charity. It is a fixed share, usually one-fortieth (2.5%) of savings that stay above a threshold for a whole lunar year, given to the groups named in 9:60. Sadaqah, voluntary charity, can be given any time, in any amount.
The word zakat carries the meaning of purifying and growing (9:103): giving cleans the heart of greed, and blessing grows in what remains.

check.q: What did the owners of the garden plan to do?
options: Share the harvest with the whole town
Pick everything at dawn so no poor person could ask for a share
check.why: They swore to reap it at dawn, quietly, so that no one in need could come in (68:17-24).

check.q: What did they find when they reached the garden?
options: The garden black and bare, as if already reaped
The poor waiting at the gate
check.why: Something from their Lord passed over it while they slept, and it was black and bare by dawn.

check.q: How much zakat is usually due on savings held for a year above the threshold?
check.why: Zakat on savings is usually one-fortieth, 2.5%, once they have stayed above the threshold for a lunar year.

check.q: What does 9:103 say charity does for the giver?
options: Purifies them and helps them grow
check.why: Charity purifies people and helps them grow (9:103).

check.q: According to the hadith, what does charity do to wealth?
check.why: The Prophet ﷺ said charity does not decrease wealth.

reflection.muslim: Look at what you have this month. Who is the person near you who needs a share of it, and how will you give it quietly?
reflection.curious: If one-fortieth of what you have were given away every year, how would it change you, and the people around you?
